problems.title: Square prism side from total surface area
problems.question: A regular square prism has total surface area 90 m² and height 6 m. Find the base side.
problems.idea: Add the two square bases and four rectangular side faces.
steps: Substitute h=6: 2a²+24a=90.
Divide by 2 and factor: a²+12a-45=(a-3)(a+15)=0.
A side is positive, so a=3.

problems.title: Distance from a prism edge to the opposite face
problems.question: A right triangular prism has all edges equal and lateral area 12 m². Find the distance from a lateral edge to the opposite lateral face.
problems.idea: The base is equilateral; the spatial distance equals its altitude.
formulas: Lateral area=base perimeter·prism height; equilateral altitude=a√3/2.
steps: If every edge is a, the lateral area is 3a·a=3a²=12, so a=2.
A lateral edge is perpendicular to the base, and the opposite face stands over the opposite base side.
Their separation is the base altitude 2√3/2=√3.

problems.title: Range after simplifying a tangent denominator
problems.question: Find the range of $y=2\sin^2x/(1+\tan^2x)$.
problems.idea: Rewrite using cosine, while retaining cosx≠0.
steps: The function is y=2sin²xcos²x=(1/2)sin²2x.
Thus 0≤y≤1/2.
Both endpoints are attained within the original domain: x=0 gives 0, and x=π/4 gives 1/2.

problems.title: A slanted section through opposite trapezoid bases
problems.question: A right prism has isosceles-trapezoid base with parallel sides 3,9 m and legs 5 m. Its height is √20 m. A plane passes through opposite parallel base edges on the two prism levels. Find its section area.
problems.idea: The section is a trapezoid whose cross-base separation combines two perpendicular distances.
formulas: Trapezoid height=√(leg²-half-base-difference²); section altitude²=base altitude²+prism height².
steps: The base trapezoid height is √(25-3²)=4.
The section’s perpendicular separation between its parallel sides is √(4²+20)=6.
Its parallel sides have lengths 3 and 9, so area=(3+9)·6/2=36.

problems.title: Largest sine root in one full turn
problems.question: Find the greatest solution of sinx=-√3/2 in (0,2π).
problems.idea: Use the reference angle π/3 in the lower half of the unit circle.
formulas: Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV.
steps: The two solutions are x=4π/3 and x=5π/3.
Both lie in the interval, and 5π/3 is greater.

problems.title: Two right triangles in perpendicular planes
problems.question: Right triangles ABP and ABQ have common hypotenuse AB and perpendicular planes. AP=AQ=3 cm,BP=BQ=4 cm. Find PQ.
problems.idea: Their right-angle vertices have the same projection on AB.
formulas: A 3-4-5 triangle has altitude to its hypotenuse h=ab/c.
steps: AB=5 and each altitude from P or Q to AB is 3·4/5=12/5.
The feet coincide because each lies distance AP²/AB=9/5 from A.
The two altitude directions are perpendicular, since the triangle planes are perpendicular.

problems.title: A box diagonal’s angles with three perpendicular planes
problems.question: A right rectangular prism’s diagonal makes angles 30° and 45° with its two lateral-face directions. Find the tangent of its angle with the base.
problems.idea: Use the perpendicular components to the three coordinate planes.
formulas: For diagonal components a,b,h and length d: (a/d)²+(b/d)²+(h/d)²=1.
steps: The two face inclinations give a/d=sin30°=1/2 and b/d=sin45°=√2/2.
The horizontal projection divided by d is √(1/4+1/2)=√3/2.
The required tangent is (1/2)/(√3/2)=1/√3.

problems.title: Which sum can belong to a prism?
problems.question: Which listed number can equal a prism’s total numbers of faces, edges and vertices: 58,59,60,61,62,63?
problems.idea: Use the general n-gonal prism counts.
steps: The total is 6n+2.
It must therefore leave remainder 2 when divided by 6.
Only 62 does so; it corresponds to n=10.

problems.title: Two complementary inverse trigonometric functions
problems.question: Find the greatest value of arccosb+arcsinb.
problems.idea: The sum is constant on its common domain.
steps: Let t=arcsinb, so -π/2≤t≤π/2.
Then cos(π/2-t)=b with π/2-t∈[0,π], hence arccosb=π/2-t.
The sum equals π/2 for every allowed b.

problems.title: Combine sine and cosine into one shifted sine
problems.question: Solve √3sinx-cosx=1 with 2π<x<5π/2.
problems.idea: Use a phase shift with amplitude 2.
steps: The equation becomes sin(x-π/6)=1/2.
Its general families are x=π/3+2πk and x=π+2πk.
Only the first family with k=1 lies in (2π,5π/2), giving x=7π/3.

problems.title: Small space diagonal of a regular hexagonal prism
problems.question: Every edge of a regular hexagonal prism is 4. Find the shorter space diagonal.
problems.idea: Its horizontal projection is the shorter hexagon diagonal.
formulas: A regular hexagon’s shorter diagonal is a√3; space distance²=horizontal distance²+height².
steps: The projection is 4√3 and the prism height is 4.
The shorter space diagonal is 8.

problems.title: Faces from a space-diagonal count
problems.question: A prism has 70 space diagonals. How many faces does it have?
problems.idea: Use the n-gonal space-diagonal formula.
steps: The positive solution is n=10.
The prism has 10+2=12 faces.

problems.title: Smallest positive root of a cosine equation
problems.question: Find the smallest positive solution of cos2x+1=cosx.
problems.idea: Use cos2x+1=2cos²x.
steps: The equation requires cosx=0 or cosx=1/2.
The smallest positive root of the first family is π/2, and of the second is π/3.
The smaller is π/3.

problems.title: Equality in the maximum sine-cosine sum
problems.question: Find the greatest solution of sinx+cosx=√2 in (0,9).
problems.idea: The sum reaches √2 only at its phase maximum.
steps: Require sin(x+π/4)=1, so x=π/4+2πk.
Within (0,9), the values are π/4 and 9π/4.
The latter is the greatest.

problems.title: Diagonal-section and lateral-area ratio
problems.question: A right prism has a rhombus base. Its two diagonal sections have area ratio 8:15. Find the smaller section divided by the lateral area.
problems.idea: The section ratio is the diagonal ratio; the half-diagonals determine the side.
formulas: Section areas=d₁h,d₂h; rhombus side=√(d₁²+d₂²)/2; lateral area=4sh.
steps: Write the diagonals as 8t,15t. Their half-lengths form an 8-15-17 ratio, giving side 17t/2.
The lateral area is 4(17t/2)h=34th.
The smaller section has area 8th, so the ratio is 8/34=4/17.

problems.title: A square-root substitution in a cosine equation
problems.question: Solve |cosx|+√(cosx)=3/4.
problems.idea: The root forces cosx≥0, so its absolute value equals itself.
steps: The equation becomes u²+u=3/4.
The roots are u=1/2 and u=-3/2; only 1/2 is allowed.
Thus cosx=1/4, giving x=±arccos(1/4)+2πk for every integer k.
problems.note: The integer k must include negative integers to describe every real solution; the source’s k=0,1,2,... restriction omits some roots.

problems.title: A nonpositive product can be nonnegative only at zero
problems.question: Solve $(\sin x-1)\sqrt{(x-8)/(16-x)}\ge0$.
problems.idea: The two factors have fixed opposite signs on the radical’s domain.
formulas: Domain: 8≤x<16; sinx-1≤0, while the square root is nonnegative.
steps: The product can be ≥0 only if one factor is zero.
The root vanishes at x=8. Otherwise require sinx=1, meaning x=π/2+2πk.
Inside (8,16), the only such value is 9π/2.
The endpoint 16 is forbidden by the denominator.

problems.title: Principal arccotangent convention
problems.question: Evaluate sin[arccot(-√3)].
problems.idea: Use the usual arccotangent range (0,π).
steps: The angle in (0,π) with cotangent -√3 is 5π/6.
Its sine is 1/2.
problems.note: Some software defines arccot on a different principal interval. Under a (-π/2,π/2) convention the angle would be -π/6 and the sine -1/2; the school convention used here is (0,π).

problems.title: Prism height from base area and lateral area
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has base area 16√3 cm² and lateral area 48 cm². Find its height.
problems.idea: Find the equilateral base side, then use its perimeter.
steps: a²√3/4=16√3 gives a²=64 and a=8.
The base perimeter is 24.

problems.title: Opposite bounds force equality
problems.question: How many roots does cosx=|x|+1 have?
problems.idea: The left side is at most 1 and the right side at least 1.
steps: Equality of the sides requires |x|+1=1, giving x=0.
At x=0, cos0=1, so it works.
There are no other candidates.

problems.title: Amplitude gives a trigonometric minimum
problems.question: Find the minimum of y=8cosx-15sinx+9.
problems.idea: A linear combination of sine and cosine has amplitude √(A²+B²).
steps: The amplitude is √(8²+15²)=17.
Thus 8cosx-15sinx has minimum -17, which is attained.
Adding 9 gives -8.

problems.title: Equivalent equations can both have no real roots
problems.question: Which listed equation is equivalent over the reals to sin(πx)=π/2?
problems.idea: The sine equation has an impossible right side.
formulas: |sinθ|≤1; a quadratic with negative discriminant has no real roots.
steps: Since π/2>1, the original equation has no real solutions.
Among the choices, x²-x+1=0 has discriminant 1-4=-3<0 and likewise no real solutions.
The two equations therefore have exactly the same empty real solution set.

problems.title: Count integers outside a function’s domain
problems.question: How many integers in [-1,10] make $\sqrt{9x^2-49}/[\sin(\pi x/2)-1]$ undefined?
problems.idea: Count failures of the radicand and denominator without double-counting.
formulas: Radicand requires |x|≥7/3; denominator must be nonzero.
steps: The integer radicand failures are -1,0,1,2: four values.
The remaining integers are 3,...,10. Among these, sin(πx/2)=1 at x=5 and 9.
Those are two further forbidden values, giving 4+2=6.

problems.title: Recover cosα from a shifted sine and an interval
problems.question: sin(60°+α)=2/3 and 70°<α<100°. Find cosα.
problems.idea: The shifted angle is in quadrant II, so its cosine is negative.
steps: Given sinθ=2/3, we have cosθ=-√(1-4/9)=-√5/3.

problems.title: A parameter must match the range of an absolute sine
problems.question: For which a does 2|sinx|=|a|-1 have at least one real solution?
problems.idea: The left side takes exactly all values in [0,2].
steps: Require 0≤|a|-1≤2.
This gives a∈[-3,-1]∪[1,3], including endpoints.
